SearchAliases: a golden-scaled fish through the net

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net figures an exceptional adept no longer caught by ordinary devices.
EvidenceBody: The phrase is anchored in Sansheng’s public question to Xuefeng: “What does the golden-scaled fish through the net feed on?” (透網金鱗未審以何為食); Xuefeng replies that he will tell him after he comes out of the net. Yuanwu’s prose supplies the corpus’s direct definition: “only with an eye at the crown is one called a golden-scaled fish through the net” (頂門有眼方謂之透網金鱗). The image then becomes an appraisal of monks: Baowen Hongyin hails a patch-robed monastic as “excellent—a patch-robed monk, a golden-scaled fish through the net” (俊哉衲子，透網金鱗), while later interviews ask why such a fish is still held up by water.
